To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the existence of the singlet fermion with the mass m s ∼ 1 eV and the mass mixing m μs ∝ O (1)  eV with the muon neutrino is a solution of the atmospheric neutrino, the solar neutrino, and the LSND problems.

(i) the see-saw mechanism with a light fermionic singlet can be a solution of the neutrino oscillation problems, (ii) the singlet can be the component of hot dark matter in our Universe, and (iii) the origin of the light singlet can be explained in the context of the left-right symmetric models.

the see-saw mechanism of neutrino mass generation can be made consistent with the solar and atmospheric neutrino experiments, and with the LSND results, if one postulates the existence of a singlet fermion which mixes predominantly with the muon neutrino.
